Everything we agreed with Uncle Chai doesn't count anymore.

Why should it be me? Why!

9198398713880300171: Fish sashimi was not only common in ancient royal courts but also a daily dish among commoners. Popular since the pre-Qin era, it's mentioned in The Book of Songs: "Feasting honored guests with roasted turtle and sliced carp." In the late Tang Dynasty, Xia Yanqian's poem "Visiting a Friend in Summer" also describes serving "silver-sliced carp on ice." Fresh fish, garnished with ginger, scallions, and mustard sauce, was widely consumed raw during the Tang and Song dynasties.
